context:
The International Space Station (ISS) is a large spacecraft that orbits Earth. It serves as a scientific research laboratory where astronauts conduct experiments in biology, physics, astronomy, and other scientific fields.

The first module of the International Space Station, called Zarya, was launched on November 20, 1998. The ISS is a collaborative project involving five major space agencies: NASA from the United States, Roscosmos from Russia, JAXA from Japan, ESA from Europe, and CSA from Canada.

The International Space Station orbits Earth at an average altitude of approximately 400 kilometers. It travels at a speed of about 28,000 kilometers per hour and completes one orbit around Earth approximately every 90 minutes.

Astronauts aboard the ISS experience microgravity, allowing scientists to investigate phenomena that are difficult to study on Earth. Research conducted on the station contributes to advances in medicine, materials science, and space exploration.

The ISS receives electricity from large solar arrays that convert sunlight into electrical energy. Its systems recycle water and help maintain a breathable atmosphere for the crew.

The station is designed to support a continuous human presence in space. The first long-duration crew arrived on November 2, 2000.
